summary: One Run, one provisioned machine, and the half of bootstrapping every earlier fixture finished too early to see: what happens to a machine after its first session credential lapses. The provider allocates in twenty two seconds, boots in three minutes eleven, and the node agent opens its session forty three seconds later, so the machine is executable about four minutes in. The Run it is then given takes forty five minutes, which is longer than one session lifetime, so the credential the agent enrolled with expires while the container is still running. What the record has to show at that moment is a renewal recorded as its own operation and no second enrolment: the invitation was redeemed once, and an agent that answered an expired credential by replaying the invitation would be presenting material the store has already spent and the signer already refuses. Nothing here is terminated, because the machine goes on working. The stage durations are deliberately not multiples of the fifteen seconds these cases reconcile at, for the reason the provisioning fixture states: a control plane dating a stage from its own look would record the polling interval as a property of the machine. The runtime is deliberately not a multiple of the session lifetime either, so the renewal lands in the middle of the work rather than on a boundary a reader could mistake for the end of the Run.
